feed.title: Testing & QA — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Sites to Test On
entry.summary: A list of target sites and APIs for practising test automation: demo shops, forms, trap-laden pages and fake APIs, grouped by kind. Rather than repeating dozens of interchangeable demo sites, this directory keeps a few representatives and points here for the rest.

entry.title: Academy Bugs
entry.summary: A practice site with 25 real bugs planted inside for you to find. Unlike automation practice sites it targets manual exploratory testing: you find the bugs and report them.

entry.title: Airport Gap
entry.summary: A RESTful API built to improve your API automation testing. Unlike simple mock APIs, it has realistic behaviour such as token authentication and rate limiting.

entry.title: API Challenges
entry.summary: A series of challenges, tutorials and references for practising API testing, by Alan Richardson (EvilTester). Unlike ordinary mock APIs it comes with a task list, marking your progress as you complete each challenge.

entry.title: Applitools
entry.summary: A visual regression testing platform that compares screens with visual AI. Unlike pixel-by-pixel tools, it ignores trivial differences such as anti-aliasing and flags real changes.

entry.title: Automation Exercise
entry.summary: An automation practice site with a UI, an API backend and a ready list of test cases. Unlike single-page demo sites, it offers end-to-end flows — sign-up, cart, checkout — together with their API.

entry.title: Awesome Appium
entry.summary: A resource list for Appium, the mobile-app test-automation tool. Unlike platform-specific tools such as Espresso or XCUITest, it drives Android and iOS from one API over the WebDriver protocol.

entry.title: Awesome AVA
entry.summary: A list of plugins and resources for AVA, the JavaScript test runner. Unlike Jest, it runs test files concurrently in separate processes by default.

entry.title: Awesome CodeRabbit
entry.summary: A resource list for CodeRabbit, the AI-powered code-review platform. Unlike general AI code-review lists, it gathers only CodeRabbit configurations and sample rules; the company maintains it itself.

entry.title: Awesome Gatling
entry.summary: A resource list for Gatling, the Scala-based load- and performance-testing framework. Unlike JMeter, you write scenarios in code (Scala, Java, Kotlin) rather than clicking them together in a GUI.

entry.title: Awesome JMeter
entry.summary: A resource list for JMeter, the load- and performance-testing tool. Unlike general performance-testing lists, it gathers only JMeter plugins, integrations and guides.

entry.title: Awesome k6
entry.summary: A resource list for k6, the developer-centric load and performance testing tool. Unlike general performance lists it focuses on one tool and its scripting ecosystem.

entry.title: Awesome Playwright
entry.summary: A list of tools, plugins and examples for the Playwright ecosystem. Unlike the official docs it brings together community tooling and real project examples.

entry.title: Awesome Regression Testing
entry.summary: A list of visual-regression tools that verify changes did not break functionality or style. Unlike unit tests, they compare screenshots and catch style breakages that code assertions cannot see.

entry.title: Awesome Selenium
entry.summary: A collection of the Selenium browser-automation framework and its surrounding tools. Unlike scattered search it gathers language bindings, grid and plugins in one place.

entry.title: Awesome Test Automation
entry.summary: A list gathering test-automation frameworks, tools and resources by language and platform. Unlike scattered searches it collects them all in one organised place.

entry.title: Awesome Testing
entry.summary: A list gathering every branch of software testing — unit, end-to-end, performance, contract — with resources. Unlike a single tool list, it pairs books and testing theory with the tools; you can also find the rest of this field’s practice sites here.

entry.title: Beeceptor
entry.summary: Spins up a mock REST endpoint in seconds and intercepts or fakes HTTP requests. Unlike writing your own mock server, it needs no code or setup.

entry.title: Browserling
entry.summary: Live-test your site across different browsers and operating systems.

entry.title: Countries GraphQL API
entry.summary: A simple public GraphQL API serving country, continent and language data, with no key required. Unlike REST-based mock APIs, it suits practising GraphQL queries and client testing.

entry.title: Cypress
entry.summary: An end-to-end testing framework that runs in the browser with live reload and time-travel debugging. Unlike Selenium the test runs in the same browser loop as the app; compared with Playwright, multi-tab and cross-browser support is more limited.

entry.title: DummyJSON
entry.summary: A fake JSON REST API offering dozens of resources for quick prototyping and test data. Unlike JSONPlaceholder it has richer data (products, carts, recipes) plus authentication, pagination and search.

entry.title: Fake Store API
entry.summary: A fake e-commerce REST API with products, carts and users for front-end prototypes. Unlike general mock APIs such as JSONPlaceholder, its data model is e-commerce-specific.

entry.title: GoREST
entry.summary: A test API with OAuth2 authentication and write support, over REST and GraphQL. Unlike read-only fake APIs it truly lets you exercise create/update flows.

entry.title: httpbin
entry.summary: An HTTP testing service that echoes headers, body and response. Unlike mock REST APIs, it tests HTTP itself — headers, cookies, redirects, compression — rather than data.

entry.title: Insomnia
entry.summary: A clean API client for REST, GraphQL and gRPC requests. Unlike Postman it is lighter and open source, and can be versioned with git.

entry.title: JSONPlaceholder
entry.summary: A zero-setup test API that returns realistic fake JSON on request. Unlike running your own mock it is instantly available — the standard for prototypes and tutorials.

entry.title: Katalon
entry.summary: A low-code test automation tool for web, API and mobile. Unlike code-first frameworks such as Playwright, it builds scenarios with record-and-playback and a visual editor, no coding needed; advanced features are paid.

entry.title: Mailtrap
entry.summary: An email sandbox that captures outgoing mail before it reaches real recipients. Unlike testing against a real SMTP server, it makes accidentally emailing a customer impossible.

entry.title: Ministry of Testing
entry.summary: A hub bringing together community, learning resources and events for software testers. Unlike tool-focused sites, it centres on the craft itself — exploratory testing, test strategy, careers.

entry.title: OMDb API
entry.summary: An API serving movie and series data, handy for tests and prototypes. Since IMDb has no public API, it is the common alternative; the free key is limited to 1,000 requests a day.

entry.title: Playwright
entry.summary: Microsoft’s cross-browser (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) automation and testing framework, driving all three from one API. Unlike Selenium, it waits automatically and talks to the browser over its own protocol rather than WebDriver.

entry.title: PokéAPI
entry.summary: A large, deeply nested REST API serving Pokémon data — popular for tests and tutorials. Unlike simple fake APIs its rich, related data model lets you exercise realistic queries.

entry.title: Postman
entry.summary: A desktop/cloud tool to build, store as collections and test API requests. Unlike curl it saves requests, holds environment variables and runs automated test sequences.

entry.title: Practice Software Testing
entry.summary: A realistic tool-shop demo with both a UI and a REST API, designed for end-to-end testing. Unlike older demos it runs on a modern stack (React + API + Swagger).

entry.title: randomuser.me
entry.summary: An API generating any number of fake users (name, address, photo). Unlike fixed fixtures it returns varied, realistic data on each call — for form and list tests.

entry.title: Reqres
entry.summary: A hosted REST API that answers AJAX requests, with pagination and delay simulation. Unlike JSONPlaceholder it can also emulate response delays and error states.

entry.title: Restful-Booker
entry.summary: A test API emulating room booking, with authentication and good docs. Unlike fake APIs it includes writes and auth — a full CRUD flow can be exercised.

entry.title: Rick and Morty API
entry.summary: A free API serving character, episode and location data over both REST and GraphQL. Unlike single-protocol APIs it exposes the same data two ways, letting you test both.

entry.title: Sauce Demo
entry.summary: A sample shopping site with ready logins for learning automation; some users deliberately misbehave. Unlike random demos its scenarios are stable and repeatable.
